intro: Stronger feelings: being fed up, not being able to stand something, not caring, and changing mood.
p.estoy harto de.consejo: The h is silent: «AR-to». A woman says «estoy harta de». A noun, an infinitive or «que» follows.
p.no soporto.consejo: It is regular in the present: «soporto», «soportas». Here it goes with a noun, an infinitive or «que».
p.me da igual.consejo: It is very common. «Me da lo mismo» means the same. «Igual» never changes here.
p.me pone de mal humor.glosa: it puts me in a bad mood
p.me pone de mal humor.consejo: You can say it with an infinitive («madrugar») or with «que» + subjunctive («que griten»).
p.me pongo triste.consejo: «Ponerse» + adjective speaks of a change: «me pongo triste», «se pone nervioso».
p.me da pena.glosa: it makes me sad; I feel sorry
p.me da pena.consejo: «Pena» is sadness. It goes with an infinitive or «que»: «me da pena irme», «me da pena que te vayas».
p.enamorado de.consejo: It goes with «de»: «estoy enamorado de ella». A woman: «enamorada».
p.enfadarse con.consejo: It is pronominal: «me enfado», «te enfadas». The person goes with «con»: «me enfado con él».
p.aburrirse.consejo: It is pronominal: «me aburro», «se aburre». The rr sounds strong: «a-bu-RRIR-se».
p.llorar.consejo: The ll sounds like y: «yo-RAR». You can also cry from laughter or joy.
p.no puedo más.consejo: A phrase of release. «Más» has an accent: it is not «mas» (but).
p.basta ya.consejo: «Basta» comes from «bastar». «Ya» adds force and urgency: «¡basta ya!».
p.ruido.consejo: The initial rr sounds strong: «RRWI-do». «Hacer ruido» means to disturb with sounds.
b1.texto:
**Estar harto de** and **no soportar** take a noun, an infinitive or **que + subjunctive**:

- Estoy harta **del ruido**.
- Estoy harto **de esperar**.
- Estoy harta **de que los vecinos hagan** ruido.
- No soporto **que me griten**.

**Me pone de mal humor** and **me da pena** work the same: **madrugar** me pone de mal humor; me da pena **que te vayas**.

**Me da igual** shows indifference: me da igual el precio; me da igual **que venga** o no.

To change mood: **me pongo** triste, **me enfado**, **me aburro**.

When it is too much: **¡no puedo más!**, **¡basta ya!**
b2.f2.texto: I am fed up with the neighbours making noise.
b2.f3.texto: I don't mind because I sleep very well.
b2.f4.texto: I can't stand them playing music at three.
b2.f7.texto: I am sorry you are like this.
b4.texto:
After these expressions you can put three things:

- **A noun**: no soporto el calor · estoy harta del ruido.
- **An infinitive**, if the one who feels and the one who acts are the same person: estoy harto de esperar · me da pena irme.
- **Que + subjunctive**, if another person acts: estoy harto de que llegues tarde · me da pena que te vayas.

**Ponerse** + adjective speaks of a change of mood: me pongo nervioso, se pone triste. Pronominal verbs say the same: me enfado, me aburro, me deprimo.

**Enamorado de**, **enfadarse con** and **harto de** always take their preposition.
b4.e0.texto: I am fed up with waiting for the bus.
b4.e1.texto: It puts me in a bad mood when they make noise.
b4.e2.texto: Sometimes I get sad for no reason.
b5.f0.texto: The rain taps the windowpanes of the flat with a stubborn patience.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía looks at the damp wall and sighs with drooping shoulders.
b5.f2.texto: Upstairs, the neighbours drag a chair across the wooden floor.
b5.f3.texto: A dry noise runs across the ceiling like a little thunder.
b5.f4.texto: The cup of coffee cools on the living room table.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo comes in with wet hair and leaves a puddle in the hallway.
b5.f6.texto: He sits down beside her and offers her a hot chocolate.
b5.f7.texto: The sweet smell of cocoa fills the room with memories.
b5.f8.texto: Little by little Lucía's shoulders relax.
b5.f9.texto: Outside, the storm moves away and leaves a clean, bright sky.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! You say «estar harto de».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «A» is not used with «harto» in this sense.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Soy triste» describes how you always are. Not a change.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That's it! «Ponerse» + adjective speaks of a change.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tener» does not go with «triste» in Spanish.
b7.pregunta: Which one shows a change of mood?
b8.o0.refuerzo: «Gritan» reports the fact. With a feeling comes the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: Well done! Another person acts: «que» and the subjunctive.
b8.pregunta: Other people shout at me. What is missing?
b9.frase: Estoy harta de que hagan ruido
b9.traduccion: I am fed up with them making noise
b10.o1.refuerzo: That is anger. «Me da igual» is the opposite.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That would be «me da pena». «Igual» is indifference.
b10.pregunta: You say «me da igual». What do you feel?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I can't stand waiting».
b12.o0.refuerzo: That would be another person getting up early. Here it is you.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Madrugo» is conjugated and here the infinitive is needed.
b12.pregunta: Getting up early bothers you. What is missing?
p.harta.consejo: The h is silent: «AR-ta». Feminine of «harto». Do not mix it up with «arte» (art).
p.hagan.consejo: Subjunctive of «hacer» for ellos or ustedes. The h is silent: «A-gan». «Hacer ruido» is to make noise.
p.pongan.consejo: Subjunctive of «poner». It comes from «pongo». «Poner música» is to play music.
p.hablado.consejo: Participle of «hablar»: «has hablado» is the perfect «you have spoken». The h is silent.
p.enfadaron.consejo: Past (preterite) of «enfadarse». It comes with «se»: «se enfadaron». The d is soft.
p.motivo.consejo: The v sounds b: «mo-TI-bo». «Sin motivo» is for no reason; the plural is «motivos».
p.terca.consejo: The c sounds k before a: «TER-ka». Feminine of «terco». «Una paciencia terca» never gives up.
p.húmeda.consejo: The h is silent and the accent is on the «u»: «U-me-da». Feminine of «húmedo».
p.suspira.consejo: The verb of «suspiro». You «suspiras» when you let out air from sadness, tiredness or relief.
p.hombros.consejo: The h is silent: «OM-bros». The singular is «hombro». «Encogerse de hombros» is to shrug.
p.caídos.consejo: From «caer» (to fall). The accent splits «a-í» into two syllables: «ka-I-dos».
p.arrastran.consejo: The rr in the middle sounds strong: «a-RRAS-tran». It means to pull something along the floor.
p.recorre.consejo: Both r's sound strong: «rre-KO-rre». It means to go along a whole place or path from end to end.
p.enfría.consejo: The accent splits «i-a» into two syllables: «en-FRI-a». Hot coffee «se enfría» if you leave it.
p.charco.consejo: The ch sounds like in «chocolate»: «CHAR-ko». After rain you step over «los charcos».
p.chocolate.consejo: In Spain «un chocolate caliente» is a thick drink. The ch sounds like in English.
p.cacao.consejo: Two c's, both k: «ka-KA-o». The «a-o» are in separate syllables, as with two strong vowels.
p.aflojan.consejo: The j sounds h: «a-FLO-han». «Aflojar» is to make less tight; it is used for muscles, knots and belts.
p.aleja.consejo: From «lejos» (far). The j sounds h. It is used with «se»: «la tormenta se aleja».
p.harto.consejo: The h is silent: «AR-to». It goes with «de»: «estar harto de». A woman says «harta».
p.griten.consejo: Subjunctive of «gritar» for ellos or ustedes. The a of «gritan» becomes e: «que me griten».
